summary.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 34% QoQ to INR112 crores and EBITDA to INR15 crores (13.4% margin), but volumes remain well below last year's Q4.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential recovery: standalone revenue of INR112 crores (up 34% QoQ) and consolidated revenue of INR110 crores (up 40% QoQ), with standalone PAT rising to INR12 crores from INR4 crores. Year-on-year the quarter was weaker, as US tariff uncertainty cut mint export volumes and utilisation fell to about 60-65% from about 80% a year earlier. The Dahej facility (Krystal Ingredients) commenced commercial production of Gemcool 5 and Safranal on February 26, 2026, while phenol-derivative production was deferred due to phenol price spikes and supply disruption. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, while reiterating FY28 targets of INR1,050-1,100 crores consolidated turnover and 16-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Mint (GEM standalone)
segments.commentary: Mint export volumes fell on US tariff uncertainty, the main driver of the YoY revenue decline; management does not disclose product-level contribution. Utilisation at GEM level dipped to about 60-65% in Q4 FY26 from about 80% in Q4 FY25.

segments.name: Clove and derivatives (Krystal)
segments.commentary: Management cited encouraging traction in clove and its derivatives, with eugenol and clove oil part of the integrated portfolio, though no separate figures were given.

segments.name: Dahej facility (Krystal Ingredients)
segments.commentary: Of about INR270 crores planned capex, nearly INR260 crores is incurred and substantially capitalised. Gemcool 5 and Safranal commercial production began February 26, 2026; the whole facility went live in April 2026.

segments.name: Phenol derivatives (Anisole etc.)
segments.commentary: Plant is production-ready with catalyst prepared, but production has not started; management held off because phenol prices spiked. Internal planning assumes a 50:50 split between captive consumption and external sale of Anisole.

guidance_outlook: FY28 targets (reiterated): consolidated turnover INR1,050-1,100 crores and EBITDA margin 16-18%.
No FY27 guidance given; management said it would be better placed to guide in one or two quarters.
Dahej asset turn expected at 3-3.5x on about INR270 crores capex, implying peak revenue potential of about INR800 crores.
Dahej utilisation not guided for FY27; management expects to share utilisation numbers around H2 FY27.
Management expects FY27 to be roughly in line with, and closer to, FY25 levels, citing removal of US tariffs and capacity additions.
capex_capacity: Dahej greenfield facility (Krystal Ingredients): about INR260 crores of about INR270 crores planned capex incurred and substantially capitalised.
Gemcool 5 and Safranal commercial production started February 26, 2026; the entire facility reported live in April 2026.
Phenol derivative plant is production-ready with catalyst prepared; start deferred until phenol prices and supply stabilise.
GEM-level utilisation about 60-65% in Q4 FY26 versus about 80% in Q4 FY25; no FY27 utilisation target given.
CMO/CDMO qualification audits by multiple customers ongoing; management expects a significant part to be completed within two quarters.
demand_pricing: Management said US tariff clarity arrived only in late February 2026, delaying Q4 export orders; order and deal flows are now reported to be returning.
Phenol supply disruption from geopolitical events forced suppliers into force majeure or delayed shipments, raising phenol prices and deferring phenol-derivative production.
Customers and distributors have qualified phenol-based product samples; management says the only gating item is phenol price stabilisation.

Cooling agents are positioned as a tariff-exempt export product (India to US) with applications in oral care and confectionery; management says they can act as boosters alongside menthol rather than fully replacing it.
Standalone GST-related headwind has passed and business has normalised, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is Dahej's revenue potential and utilisation target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an asset turn of 3-3.5x on the capex, giving peak revenue of about INR800 crores. No FY27 utilisation guidance; a number is expected around H2 as the plant ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 FY26 weaker than Q4 FY25 despite expected restocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US tariff clarity only came in late February 2026, so Q4 export ramp-up slipped. Management expects this to materialise from the current quarter onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the phenol plant not start, and can phenol be imported?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said phenol prices spiked around March and suppliers issued force majeure, so it chose to wait for a new price equilibrium before starting a continuous plant. Imports are possible but were deemed too costly at the time.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 45-46% YoY revenue decline when US exports are about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the comparison is Q4 vs Q4, and Q4 is seasonally the largest quarter, heavily weighted to US exports. FY26 export share was 44% and domestic 56%; the exact Q4 US share was to be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give FY27 standalone revenue and EBITDA guidance (for example 15-17% margin and about INR700 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide for FY27 given geopolitical uncertainty and raw-material volatility, and said it would be better placed to guide in one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can synthetic volumes shift to natural products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the same hardware can make some products both ways, but others need extra equipment; it is in 70 standalone SKUs and does not disclose the natural/synthetic split.

risks_watch: Phenol price and availability: phenol-derivative production start is contingent on price stabilisation; management acknowledged this could affect near-term timelines.
Export dependence on the US: tariff clarity arrived late and Q4 volumes fell sharply YoY; US export share in Q4 was not disclosed on the call.
Standalone utilisation fell to about 60-65% from about 80%; watch for recovery in H2 FY27.
Heavy depreciation from capitalisation of Dahej is weighing on consolidated profitability; consolidated PAT was only INR1 crore.
Management declined to guide FY27; the Q1 FY27 update and any FY27 guidance will be key checkpoints.
Pending CMO/CDMO qualification audits at Dahej: management expects significant progress within two quarters.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident about the long-term story and the sequential recovery, but noticeably cautious on FY27, repeatedly citing geopolitical and raw-material uncertainty. It deferred on specific questions: utilisation, product-level margins, natural versus synthetic mix, and US export share. Answers on the Q4 YoY decline and phenol timing were defensive and sometimes unclear.
key_quotes: Q4 FY '26 marked a quarter of sequential improvement for the company, reflecting gradual recovery in the operating environment and improving business momentum across key markets.
So it'll be difficult for us to give a FY '27 guidance at this stage.
We believe these challenges are temporary in nature and expect conditions to gradually improve as external issues soften.
